title: RRB NTPC CBT-1 — Full-Length Railway Recruitment Mock Paper
subtitle: 100 Questions • 90 Minutes • 100 Marks • Official +1 / -0.33 (1/3rd) Marking
description: Exact full-length Railway Recruitment Board (RRB) NTPC CBT-1 replica modelled on official CEN 01/2019 & NTPC shifts: General Awareness (40 Qs), Mathematics (30 Qs), and General Intelligence & Reasoning (30 Qs) in 90 minutes with +1 / -1/3rd negative marking.
instructions: Exact RRB NTPC CBT-1 pattern: 100 objective MCQs (100 marks) in 90 minutes composite duration.
Sectional distribution: General Awareness (40 Qs) • Mathematics (30 Qs) • General Intelligence & Reasoning (30 Qs).
Official Railway marking scheme: +1 mark per correct answer and -1/3rd (-0.33) negative marking for every wrong answer.

questions.question: Between which two stations did India's first passenger train run on 16 April 1853?
questions.explanation: India's first passenger train ran 34 km from Bori Bunder (now Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus) to Thane on 16 April 1853.

questions.question: Where is the headquarters of the South Central Railway (SCR) zone located?
questions.explanation: South Central Railway (SCR) is headquartered at Rail Nilayam, Secunderabad (Telangana).

questions.question: Which railway station in India currently holds the Guinness World Record for the world's longest railway platform (1,507 m)?
questions.explanation: Hubballi Junction (Karnataka, South Western Railway) has the world's longest railway platform at 1,507 metres, inaugurated in March 2023.

questions.question: The Integral Coach Factory (ICF), which manufactures Vande Bharat Express trainsets, is situated in:
questions.explanation: ICF is located in Perambur, Chennai (Tamil Nadu); RCF is in Kapurthala, MCF in Raebareli, and CLW in Chittaranjan.

questions.question: Who was the first Governor-General of independent India?
questions.explanation: Lord Mountbatten was the first Governor-General of independent India (1947–48); C. Rajagopalachari was the first and only Indian Governor-General.

questions.question: The Non-Cooperation Movement was called off by Mahatma Gandhi in February 1922 following which incident?
questions.explanation: After a violent clash at Chauri Chaura (Gorakhpur, UP) on 4 February 1922, Gandhiji suspended the Non-Cooperation Movement.

questions.question: Who composed the 'Arthashastra', the ancient Indian treatise on statecraft and economic policy?
questions.explanation: Kautilya (Chanakya / Vishnugupta), chief advisor to Chandragupta Maurya, authored the Arthashastra.

questions.question: In which year was the First Battle of Panipat fought between Babur and Ibrahim Lodi?
questions.explanation: Babur defeated Ibrahim Lodi in the First Battle of Panipat on 21 April 1526, founding the Mughal Empire.

questions.question: How many Schedules are currently present in the Constitution of India?
questions.explanation: Originally there were 8 Schedules; subsequent amendments expanded the Constitution to 12 Schedules.

questions.question: Which Article empowers the President of India to promulgate Ordinances when Parliament is not in session?
questions.explanation: Article 123 grants ordinance-making power to the President (Article 213 grants the analogous power to State Governors).

questions.question: Who is the Guardian of the Public Purse and audits all receipts and expenditure of the Union and States under Article 148?
questions.explanation: The CAG of India (Article 148) heads the Indian Audit and Accounts Department.

questions.question: Which Constitutional Amendment gave constitutional status to Panchayati Raj Institutions (Part IX)?
questions.explanation: The 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act (1992) added Part IX and the Eleventh Schedule for Panchayati Raj.

questions.question: Which is the highest mountain peak located entirely within India (undisputed Indian territory)?
questions.explanation: Nanda Devi (7,816 m in Uttarakhand) is the highest peak entirely inside India; Kangchenjunga (8,586 m) lies on the India-Nepal border.

questions.question: Which strait separates India from Sri Lanka?
questions.explanation: The Palk Strait connects the Bay of Bengal with the Gulf of Mannar, separating Tamil Nadu from Sri Lanka.

questions.question: Hirakud Dam, one of the longest earthen dams in the world, is constructed across which river?
questions.explanation: Hirakud Dam is built across the Mahanadi River near Sambalpur in Odisha.

questions.question: Black soil (Regur soil), rich in clay and moisture-retentive, is most ideal for cultivating which crop?
questions.explanation: Deccan Trap black (Regur) soil is famously known as Black Cotton Soil.

questions.question: What is the SI unit of Power?
questions.explanation: Power = Work / Time, measured in Joules per second = Watt (W).

questions.question: Light year is a unit used to measure:
questions.explanation: One light year is the distance light travels in vacuum in one Julian year ($\approx 9.46 \times 10^{15}\text{ m}$).

questions.question: Which lens is prescribed to correct Myopia (nearsightedness)?
questions.explanation: A diverging (concave) lens shifts the image backward onto the retina to correct Myopia.

questions.question: Which gas is filled in electric filament bulbs along with argon to prevent oxidation of the tungsten filament?
questions.explanation: Inert Nitrogen and Argon suppress filament evaporation and prevent tungsten oxidation.

questions.question: Brass is an alloy primarily composed of which two metals?
questions.explanation: Brass = Copper + Zinc (whereas Bronze = Copper + Tin).

questions.question: Which isotope of Carbon is used in radiocarbon dating to estimate the age of ancient organic fossils?
questions.explanation: Radioactive $^{14}\text{C}$ (half-life ~5,730 years) is used in radiocarbon dating.

questions.question: Which organelle is called the 'Powerhouse of the Cell' because it generates ATP via cellular respiration?
questions.explanation: Mitochondria synthesize ATP (adenosine triphosphate) through oxidative phosphorylation.

questions.question: Malaria is caused by the protozoan parasite *Plasmodium* and transmitted to humans by the bite of:
questions.explanation: Female *Anopheles* mosquitoes transmit Malaria (*Aedes aegypti* transmits Dengue/Chikungunya).

questions.question: Which is the largest gland in the human body?
questions.explanation: The Liver is the largest internal organ and largest gland in the human body.

questions.question: Which of the following is a volatile primary memory in a computer?
questions.explanation: RAM (Random Access Memory) loses all stored data when power is turned off (volatile).

questions.question: In computer terminology, 1 Kilobyte (KB) in binary IEC/classic railway exam convention equals:
Who is widely regarded as the 'Father of the Computer' for designing the Analytical Engine?
questions.explanation: Charles Babbage designed the Difference Engine and Analytical Engine in the 19th century.

questions.question: Which shortcut key is universally used in Windows/office applications to 'Undo' the last action?
questions.explanation: `Ctrl + Z` performs Undo (`Ctrl + Y` performs Redo).

questions.question: Which type of tax is the Goods and Services Tax (GST) in India?
questions.explanation: GST is a comprehensive, multi-stage, destination-based indirect tax on the supply of goods and services.

questions.question: The National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development (NABARD) was established in 1982 on the recommendation of which committee?
questions.explanation: NABARD was set up on 12 July 1982 following the B. Sivaraman Committee recommendation.

questions.question: Where is the headquarters of the United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization (UNESCO) located?
questions.explanation: UNESCO is headquartered in Paris, France.

questions.question: How many permanent members with veto power sit on the United Nations Security Council (UNSC)?
questions.explanation: The five permanent members (P5) are China, France, Russia, the United Kingdom, and the United States.

questions.question: India's Chandrayaan-3 Vikram lander achieved a historic soft landing near the Moon's south pole on which date (now celebrated as National Space Day)?
questions.explanation: Chandrayaan-3 touched down on 23 August 2023 at Shiv Shakti Point; India observes 23 August as National Space Day.

questions.question: What is the name of India's first dedicated solar observatory mission launched by ISRO to the Sun-Earth L1 point?
questions.explanation: Aditya-L1 was launched on 2 September 2023 aboard PSLV-C57 to study the Sun's corona and solar winds from L1.

questions.question: Ajanta and Ellora Caves, renowned for Buddhist, Hindu, and Jain rock-cut monuments, are located in which district of Maharashtra?
questions.explanation: Both UNESCO World Heritage sites lie in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar (formerly Aurangabad) district, Maharashtra.

questions.question: Who was the first Indian woman to win two Olympic medals (silver at Rio 2016 and bronze at Tokyo 2020)?
questions.explanation: Badminton star P. V. Sindhu became the first Indian woman to win two individual Olympic medals.

questions.question: The 'Ramsar Convention' (1971) is an international treaty dedicated to the conservation and sustainable use of:
questions.explanation: Signed in Ramsar, Iran (2 Feb 1971), the Ramsar Convention protects Wetlands of International Importance.

questions.question: Which Indian classical language was the VERY FIRST to be declared a Classical Language by the Government of India in 2004?
questions.explanation: Tamil was declared India's first Classical Language in 2004, followed by Sanskrit in 2005.

questions.question: Who wrote 'The Discovery of India' while imprisoned at Ahmednagar Fort?
questions.explanation: Jawaharlal Nehru wrote 'The Discovery of India' during 1942–1946 at Ahmednagar Fort.

questions.question: Evaluate: $96 \div 8 + 14 \times 3 - 18$
How many prime numbers lie strictly between 20 and 50?
Find the smallest number which when divided by 12, 15, and 20 leaves a remainder of 5 in each case.
Express the recurring decimal $0.\overline{36}$ as a simplified fraction.
What is the fourth proportional to 6, 9, and 16?
questions.explanation: $6 : 9 :: 16 : x \Rightarrow x = \frac{9 \times 16}{6} = 24$.

questions.question: A town's population increases by 10% every year. If its present population is 20,000, what will it be after 2 years?
If the cost price of 15 pens equals the selling price of 12 pens, find the gain percentage.
In how many years will ₹4,000 yield ₹1,440 as simple interest at 9% per annum?
A sum doubles in 4 years at compound interest. In how many years will it become 8 times itself at the same rate?
questions.explanation: $8 = 2^3$, so time = $3 \times 4 = 12$ years.

questions.question: A can do a job in 16 days and B in 24 days. With the help of C, they complete it in 6 days. In how many days can C alone do the job?
questions.explanation: Work = 48. A=3, B=2, A+B+C=8 ⇒ C=3 units/day ⇒ C alone takes $48/3 = 16$ days.

questions.question: Tap A fills a cistern in 10 hours and Tap B empties it in 15 hours. If both are opened together, in how many hours will the empty cistern be full?
questions.explanation: Net rate = $\frac{1}{10} - \frac{1}{15} = \frac{1}{30}$ per hour ⇒ 30 hours.

questions.question: A 250 m long train running at 54 km/h crosses a 350 m long bridge in how many seconds?
questions.explanation: Speed = $15\text{ m/s}$. Total distance = $600\text{ m}$. Time = $600 / 15 = 40$ s.

questions.question: The average of 7 numbers is 24. If one number is excluded, the average of the remaining 6 numbers becomes 22. What was the excluded number?
questions.explanation: Excluded = $7\times 24 - 6\times 22 = 168 - 132 = 36$.

questions.question: Find the area of a right-angled triangle whose base is 18 cm and hypotenuse is 30 cm.
questions.explanation: Height = $\sqrt{30^2 - 18^2} = 24\text{ cm}$. Area = $\frac{1}{2} \times 18 \times 24 = 216\text{ cm}^2$.

questions.question: Find the length of the longest rod that can be placed inside a cuboid room of dimensions $12\text{ m} \times 9\text{ m} \times 8\text{ m}$.
questions.explanation: Space diagonal = $\sqrt{12^2 + 9^2 + 8^2} = \sqrt{144 + 81 + 64} = \sqrt{289} = 17\text{ m}$.

questions.question: Find the arithmetic mean of the dataset: `14, 18, 22, 26, 30, 34`.
Find the **median** of the observations: `15, 8, 23, 12, 19, 7, 21`.
If the Mean of a moderately skewed distribution is 28 and the Median is 26, find the approximate **Mode** using the empirical formula.
If the variance of a dataset is 169, what is its standard deviation?
questions.explanation: Standard Deviation = $\sqrt{\text{Variance}} = \sqrt{169} = 13$.

questions.question: If $a + b = 9$ and $ab = 14$, find $a^2 + b^2$.
Find the sum of the roots of the quadratic equation $2x^2 - 14x + 19 = 0$.
questions.explanation: Sum of roots = $-\frac{b}{a} = \frac{14}{2} = 7$.

questions.question: Two supplementary angles are in the ratio $4 : 5$. Find the smaller angle.
questions.explanation: $4x + 5x = 180^\circ \Rightarrow x = 20^\circ$. Smaller angle = $4 \times 20^\circ = 80^\circ$.

questions.question: Each exterior angle of a regular polygon measures $40^\circ$. How many sides does the polygon have?
questions.explanation: Number of sides $n = \frac{360^\circ}{40^\circ} = 9$ (nonagon).

questions.question: If $\tan\theta = \frac{3}{4}$ (for acute $\theta$), find the value of $\sin\theta + \cos\theta$.
questions.explanation: Hypotenuse = $\sqrt{3^2+4^2}=5$. $\sin\theta = 3/5$, $\cos\theta = 4/5 \Rightarrow \text{sum} = 7/5$.

questions.question: Find the value of $\frac{\sin 38^\circ}{\cos 52^\circ} + \frac{\tan 25^\circ}{\cot 65^\circ}$.
questions.explanation: $\sin 38^\circ = \cos 52^\circ$ and $\tan 25^\circ = \cot 65^\circ$, so $1 + 1 = 2$.

questions.question: The shadow of a vertical pole of height 15 m is $15\sqrt{3}\text{ m}$ long. What is the angle of elevation of the Sun?
questions.explanation: $\tan\theta = \frac{15}{15\sqrt{3}} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}} \Rightarrow \theta = 30^\circ$.

questions.question: A and B invest ₹15,000 and ₹25,000 respectively for 1 year. If total profit is ₹16,000, find A's profit share.
A mother is 3 times as old as her daughter. After 12 years, she will be twice as old as her daughter. What is the daughter's present age?
questions.explanation: $3x + 12 = 2(x + 12) \Rightarrow x = 12$ years.

questions.question: Evaluate: $\sqrt{0.0625} + \sqrt{0.0225}$

Passenger tickets (in thousands) booked at a railway zone over 4 quarters:

| Quarter | Q1 | Q2 | Q3 | Q4 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Tickets (k)** | 120 | 150 | 180 | 150 |

What percentage of the annual bookings occurred in **Q3**?
`Heart : Cardiologist :: Kidney : ?`
questions.explanation: A Nephrologist specializes in kidney diseases.

questions.question:
Find the missing number:
`9, 16, 25, 36, 49, ?`

Complete the series:
`B, E, H, K, N, ?`
questions.explanation: Each letter advances by +3: N(14) + 3 = Q(17).

questions.question: If `TRAIN` is coded as `WUDLQ`, how is `METRO` coded?
questions.explanation: Each letter shifts +3: M→P, E→H, T→W, R→U, O→R ⇒ `PHWUR`.

questions.question:
If `×` means `+`, `÷` means `-`, `+` means `×`, and `-` means `÷`, find:
`20 - 4 + 3 × 8 ÷ 5`

Statements:
1. All trains are vehicles.
2. Some vehicles are electric.

Conclusions:
I. Some vehicles are trains.
II. All electric things are trains.
questions.explanation: From Statement 1, 'Some vehicles are trains' (I) definitely follows; II does not.

questions.question: In a group of 50 commuters, 32 travel by Metro, 28 travel by Bus, and every commuter uses at least one of the two. How many use BOTH Metro and Bus?

Question: How is Ravi related to Suman?
Statements:
I. Ravi is the only son of Suman's mother.
II. Suman is a female.

Which statements are sufficient to answer the question?
options: Both I and II together are needed
Neither I nor II is sufficient
questions.explanation: From I alone, Ravi could be Suman himself (if Suman is male) or Suman's brother (if Suman is female). Statement II confirms Suman is female, making Ravi definitively her brother. Hence **Both I and II together** are required.

questions.question:
Statement: All high-speed Vande Bharat trains have automatic sliding doors for passenger safety.
Conclusions:
I. Automatic sliding doors enhance passenger safety.
II. Ordinary local passenger trains do not have any safety features.
questions.explanation: Conclusion I follows directly from the statement; II makes an unsupported generalization about ordinary trains.

questions.question:
Statement: A railway notice reads: "Please do not cross railway tracks; use the foot overbridge."
Assumptions:
I. Some passengers tend to cross railway tracks directly.
II. A foot overbridge is available at the station.
options: Both I and II are implicit
Neither I nor II is implicit
questions.explanation: Issuing the warning assumes passengers might cross tracks (I) and that a foot overbridge exists for them to use (II).

questions.question: A is the father of B, but B is not the son of A. How is B related to A?
questions.explanation: If A is B's father and B is not his son, B must be his **Daughter**.

questions.question: Mohan walks 10 m South, turns left and walks 15 m, then turns left again and walks 10 m. How far and in which direction is he from the start?
questions.explanation: 10 m South and 10 m North cancel; turning left from South goes East ⇒ **15 m East**.

questions.question: Select the odd word from the given alternatives.
questions.explanation: Copper, Aluminium, and Iron are metals; Wood is a non-metallic organic insulator.

questions.question: Rearrange the jumbled letters `A R N I T` to form a meaningful English word. What is the middle letter of that word?
questions.explanation: Unscrambled word = `TRAIN`. Middle (3rd) letter is `A`.

questions.question: In a row of 40 passengers, Rajesh is 14th from the right end. What is his position from the left end?

questions.explanation: $n : n(n+1) \Rightarrow 7 \times 8 = 56$, so $9 \times 10 = 90$.

questions.question:
Find the missing number:
`3, 10, 29, 66, 127, ?`
If `E = 5` and `PEN = 35`, then `PAGE = ?`
If today is Tuesday, what day of the week will it be after 64 days?
questions.explanation: $64 \bmod 7 = 1$ odd day. Tuesday + 1 = **Wednesday**.

questions.question: How many times do the hands of a standard clock coincide (overlap at $0^\circ$) in a 12-hour period?
questions.explanation: The hands coincide 11 times in 12 hours (22 times in 24 hours), because between 11 and 1 they coincide only once at 12:00.

questions.question: Six people A, B, C, D, E, and F sit in a circle facing the centre. A sits between B and F. D sits opposite to A. C sits immediately to the right of D. E sits opposite to B. Who sits immediately to the left of D?
questions.explanation: With A opposite D, and B/F adjacent to A, C/E are adjacent to D. Since C is immediately right of D, **E** sits immediately to the left of D.

questions.question: Find the odd number out.
questions.explanation: 17, 23, and 29 are prime numbers; $39 = 3 \times 13$ is composite.

questions.question: Five cities P, Q, R, S, and T are compared by population: P has more people than Q, R has fewer people than S, T has more people than S, and Q has more people than T. Which city has the **highest** population?
questions.explanation: Order: `P > Q > T > S > R`. Highest = **P**.

questions.question: `Author : Novel :: Sculptor : ?`
questions.explanation: An author creates a novel; a sculptor creates a statue.

questions.question: Pick the odd letter-cluster out.
questions.explanation: AEI, IOU, and OUA consist exclusively of vowels; BCD consists of consonants.

questions.question:
Statements:
1. No fruit is a vegetable.
2. All apples are fruits.

Conclusions:
I. No apple is a vegetable.
II. Some fruits are apples.
questions.explanation: Apples ⊂ Fruits and Fruits ∩ Vegetables = ∅ ⇒ No apple is a vegetable (I) and Some fruits are apples (II). Both follow.

questions.question: One morning after sunrise, Vikram and Ajay were standing face-to-face talking. Vikram's shadow fell exactly to Ajay's left. Which direction was Vikram facing?
questions.explanation: In the morning, the Sun is in the East so shadows fall West. West is to Ajay's left ⇒ Ajay faces North ⇒ facing Ajay, Vikram faces **South**.

questions.question:
Find the missing term in the series:
`2, 5, 11, 23, 47, ?`

Question: What is the weight of Box X?
Statements:
I. Box X weighs 5 kg more than Box Y.
II. Total weight of Box X and Box Y is 35 kg.

Which statements are sufficient?
options: Both I and II together are sufficient
Even together they are not sufficient
questions.explanation: $X - Y = 5$ and $X + Y = 35 \Rightarrow 2X = 40 \Rightarrow X = 20\text{ kg}$. Both together are sufficient.

questions.question: How many capital English letters among `A, H, M, P, T, V, W` appear identical in a vertical plane mirror?
questions.explanation: `A, H, M, T, V, W` (6 letters) are horizontally symmetric; `P` reverses in a vertical mirror.
